recentKeyChanges.title: Optimus production confirmed for late July/August 2026 at Fremont
recentKeyChanges.description: During Tesla's Q1 2026 earnings call, Elon Musk confirmed that Optimus humanoid robot production will commence in late July or August 2026 at the Fremont factory. The facility, converted from Model S/X production (final vehicles produced May 2026), targets 1 million units annually. Musk cautioned that initial output will be 'quite slow' due to 10,000 unique parts across an entirely new production line. Tesla is simultaneously constructing a second-generation Optimus facility at Giga Texas targeting 10 million units per year, with production starting summer 2027.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Official Tesla Manufacturing video shows S/X line fully decommissioned in 46 days and floor cleared for Optimus — concrete execution progress toward the late July/August full-scale start already on the timeline.

recentKeyChanges.title: Tesla completes 46-day Model S/X line teardown for Optimus at Fremont
recentKeyChanges.description: Tesla Manufacturing posted a video on July 10, 2026 showing the original Model S and Model X assembly line at Fremont decommissioned in just 46 days — concrete pits, robotic arms, and conveyors removed. The post, captioned 'End of an era,' confirms the floor is being repurposed for Optimus. Limited Gen 3 production is already underway; full-scale output on the converted line remains targeted for late July or August 2026 with a long-term capacity ambition of 1 million units per year at Fremont.

recentKeyChanges.title: Musk warns Optimus production will be 'extremely slow' as July start approaches
recentKeyChanges.description: On July 1, 2026, Elon Musk visited the Optimus production line at Fremont and shared a team photo, responding to speculation by stating 'Optimus production will be extremely slow at first because everything is new.' This directly contradicts earlier optimism and occurs just weeks before the planned late July/August production start. Musk emphasized 'this is not like making a car' due to 10,000 unique parts. Production is expected to ramp from dozens per week in June to 100-150 per week in July, 300 per week in August, and a target of 1,000 units per week by September 2026 according to supplier reports. However, all 2026 units will be for internal testing only, not commercial customers.

sentiment.headline: neutral
sentiment.rationale: Musk's 'extremely slow' warning just weeks before production start signals significant challenges. Despite supplier targets of 1,000 units/week by September, Musk's public caution indicates these are aspirational. The reality is Tesla missed 2025 targets entirely (aimed for ~10,000 units, delivered zero commercial units), and current deployed units do no productive work. 'Everything is new' admission shows unproven production process at scale.

positive_signals: Production line operational at Fremont (Musk visited July 1, 2026)
